intent: Give OctoForge (~/octoforge) an on-style launcher icon from the shared family, replacing the stock Flutter logo it was still shipping. Registers it as app #10 with a new anvil glyph.
scope: python_pkg/app_icons/glyphs.py: adds the _ANVIL fragment and its GLYPHS entry
python_pkg/app_icons/apps.py: adds the octoforge AppIcon registry entry
Non-goal: no change to style.py, the renderer, or any existing app's icon - a style change would restyle the whole family
Non-goal: no iOS assets; OctoForge cannot be built for iOS here (no Xcode)
changes: Anvil drawn as a filled silhouette rather than a stroked outline: at the family's 72px stroke weight the narrow waist closes up solid at 48dp. Same reasoning as the existing quill-nib and receipt-split glyphs.

The horn is a separate wedge projecting off the face, tapering to a 40px blunt tip (above MIN_NEGATIVE_SPACE so it survives at launcher size). Two earlier drafts folded the taper into the face slab and rendered as a bump, leaving the shape reading as an I-beam.
Registered with linux=True: OctoForge has a real desktop target with a .desktop entry, unlike the phone-first apps that scaffolded linux/ but ship no entry.
Accent is the shared #B8862E, matching all nine existing apps - apps are distinguished by glyph shape, not colour.

verification.evidence: All hooks Passed or Skipped, including ruff, mypy, pylint, bandit, 'pytest with coverage enforcement' and 'Block binary/image files'.
44 passed; every app_icons module at 100% (apps.py, glyphs.py, cli.py, generate.py, preview.py, render.py, style.py). Registry tests are data-driven so they cover the new entry.
Wrote 6 asset files, 8 hicolor PNGs and regenerated the Android mipmaps with no safe-box warning. All five mipmap-*/ic_launcher.png md5s changed from the stock Flutter values.
Inspected the three rows (full size, circle-masked, 48dp). The anvil is legible at 48dp and sits with the family in weight and style.

verification.command: adb -s 23181JEGR08034 install -r app-debug.apk && open the app drawer
verification.evidence: Icon renders correctly in the launcher on the physical device, next to todo's checklist glyph on the same charcoal field.

risks: Glyph legibility is a visual judgement; it was checked on the preview sheet at 48dp and in the real device app drawer, not asserted by a test.

Committed from a temporary git worktree because the working tree held another session's in-flight kuhylog registry entry in the same hunk. Only the anvil and octoforge additions are in this commit; the kuhylog work is untouched and still uncommitted in the main checkout.

app-icon/SKILL.md still documents charcoal #1B1D21 and accent #4C7DF0, which the live generator and all ten registered apps contradict. Following the skill text literally would produce an off-palette icon. Not fixed here.
rollback: git revert the commit; it only adds a glyph and a registry entry, so nothing else depends on it.
After rollback, run python3 -m python_pkg.app_icons list and confirm nine apps and nine glyphs, then re-run the app_icons test suite.
OctoForge's already-generated icon assets live in its own repo and are unaffected by a revert here; regenerating them would then fail with 'unknown app octoforge', which is the expected signal.
